name: Learn basic photo editing
blurb: A repeatable editing workflow — exposure, white balance, contrast, colour, local adjustments, crop — takes competent photos to good ones without making them look processed.
gear: Lightroom, Darktable, Capture One or a phone editor
RAW files, which hold far more editable information than JPEGs
steps: Shoot RAW and understand why: far more recoverable highlight and shadow detail.
Establish a fixed order: white balance, exposure, highlights and shadows, contrast, then colour, then local adjustments, then crop and sharpen last.
Learn the tone curve, which gives finer control than the basic sliders.
Learn local adjustments: masks, gradients and brushes to lift a face or darken a sky.
Learn colour grading with HSL, adjusting individual colours rather than the whole image.
Edit the same image three ways, leave it a day, and pick which still looks right.
tips: Over-editing is the beginner signature: crushed blacks, oversaturated skies, heavy clarity. Come back the next day before publishing.
Build presets from your own repeated edits rather than buying someone else’s look.
proof: You take a flat RAW file to a finished image in under five minutes with a workflow you can repeat.
